plot: On Hal's first Monday as the library truck he must park on busy Main Street before story time at three, but every try ends with a jump and a bonk while Turbo honks his 'cheering honks', Bertha's thirty kids blow toy horns and Hal hides behind the bakery to give up; there Bolt and Pip see him park perfectly when nobody is watching (as Pip saw at the orchard at sunrise), and when Turbo's practice honks make his wheels jump again Bolt realises the problem is not Hal but the honking; Turbo says sorry, the town cheers silently with blinking lights, Hal parks like a ribbon and reads the first story, then a purple tractor rolls in asking for Turbo, a week early.

script.title: 100 Honks and Hal Still Can't Park!
script.description: Hal's first day as the library truck: he must park on Main Street before story time. Inspector Bolt #34

set.place: Wheelburg Main Street outside the little library and the back yard of Benny's bakery, a sunny Monday from late morning until three o'clock

beats.say: Back... back... oh no! Too far again!
I can't park with everyone watching! And the books are late!
Story time starts at three, Hal. Can you park by then?
It was Monday morning. Hal's very first day as the library truck.
And Main Street was very busy. And very, very loud.
Come on, Hal! Honk honk! That means GO!
Turbo. That honk sounded like a goose in a hurry.
It's a cheering honk! My best one! Honk honk honk!
Thanks, Turbo. I think.
Hal, the space is between those two cones. Take your time.
Hal backed up. Beep. Beep. Beep.
You can do it, Hal! Honk! HONK!
Hal's wheels jumped. He bumped a cone. Bonk.
See? I'm a terrible parker. The worst in Wheelburg.
But Hal! At sunrise I saw a big green truck.
At the orchard. Parked between two apple trees. Perfectly!
Oh. That was... nothing. Just some old truck.
Hal, if the books aren't in by three, I need another driver.
Another driver? But I love books. I read every night!
Don't worry! I'll show you. Zoom in fast, stop fast!
Turbo zoomed into the space. Screech! Perfect. Everyone honked.
Ta-da! See? Easy peasy! Now you, Hal!
Turbo is small. Hal is long. Like a sandwich and a sausage.
Hal is the sausage!
Hal tried again. All the cars on Main Street stopped to watch.
Honk honk! You've got this, Hal! HONK!
Hal's wheels jumped again. Bonk. The other cone.
Sorry, Mrs. Page. Maybe I'm just too big for this town.
It's two o'clock, Hal. One hour left. The children are waiting.
Then Bertha came back. With thirty kids for story time!
Look, kids! Hal is parking! Everybody cheer!
Thirty kids cheered. And thirty kids honked their toy horns.
Thirty more watching? Oh no. Oh no, no, no.
Hal. I can tow you in. One minute. Done.
Thank you, Grumpy. But I want to do it myself.
I understand. Nobody could stop me on my day off either.
So Hal tried one more time. Everyone held their breath.
This is it! The big one! HONK HONK HONK!
Hal's wheels jumped. Straight up. He nearly hit the library!
Oh dear! My books! My lovely books!
That's it. I'm not a library truck. I'm an apple truck.
Hal drove off and hid behind Benny's bakery. All alone.
Bolt, he's giving up! And the kids are waiting!
Pip. Come with me. And this time, no honking at all.
Bolt and Pip crept round the bakery. Quiet as two mice.
Shh! Look! What is Hal doing back there?
Hal was all alone. Nobody watching. Nobody honking.
Just for practice. Back... a little left... and stop.
And Hal slid between two bread crates. Perfectly. Like a ribbon.
Bolt! He CAN park! Just like at the orchard!
Then why can't he park on Main Street?
Back on Main Street, the honking started again. Turbo was practising.
Honk honk! Cheering practice! For when Hal comes back!
Ten minutes to story time! Where is Hal?
Behind the bakery, Hal heard the honks. And his wheels jumped.
Honk, then jump. Every single time. Pip, do you see it?
Hal isn't a bad parker. The honks make him jumpy!
Exactly. The problem isn't Hal. The problem is us.
Bolt and Pip raced back to Main Street.
Everyone! Please! No more honking!
But honking is cheering! Isn't it?
Not for Hal. Honks make his wheels jump. Bonk!
Oh. My cheering honks made it harder?
Hal rolled back slowly. He had heard everything.
Hal, I'm sorry. I wanted to help. I was too loud.
You were cheering for me? That's kind, Turbo. Thank you.
New plan. Silent cheering. My speciality.
Kids! Toy horns away! Wave your wheels instead!
And I'll blink my lights. Blink blink means GO, Hal!
Main Street went quiet. Not one honk. Only one little bird.
Back... a little left... and stop.
And Hal slid between the cones. Perfect. Like a ribbon.
Everyone blinked their lights and waved their wheels. Very quietly.
Just in time! Story time can start!
Mrs. Page, may I read the very first story?
When a friend is learning, cheer quietly. Give them room.
Silent cheering. Best kind of cheering.
Then a long purple tractor rolled slowly into Main Street.
Hello, Wheelburg! Which one of you is Turbo?
You're Grandma Rosa's racer?! But you're a week early!
What do you think Bolt will find next time? We'll find out in the next episode!

"I can park. Really, I can. Just... not when the whole street is watching." — Hal
It's Hal's first day as Wheelburg's library truck, and he has to park on busy Main Street before story time at three. Every try ends in a bonk. Can Inspector Bolt find out why? Inspector Bolt #34
